messages:
Maya Chen: Need a tiny, 1-page "field pocket-sheet" for AEs to drop in meetings — focused on enterprise security + SLA + deploy-mode guidance. Short enough to share in a calendared pre-demo email.

Jon Patel: Love it. Target length = single front-and-back PDF?

Maya Chen: Single front only if we can make copy razor. Front = 3 sections: 1) security proof points (KMS, audit logs, SOC2), 2) SLA and predictability bullets, 3) deploy-mode quick-check (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Bottom CTA for demos/benchmarks.

Priya Nair: Suggestion: lead with a one-line value prop for security folks — "Predictable inference, enterprise controls" then 3 micro-claims w/ one data point each (e.g., "<20ms p95 on ded. pools" - if we can validate).

Evan Li: We should avoid raw numbers unless validated. How about "typical p95 under 50ms on Reserved" and mark it as "projected on standard benchmarks" ? Also include routing fallback note: "auto-fallback to low-latency variants".

Alex G: I'm drafting the micro-claims. Also propose a tiny matrix that maps use-case -> recommended deploy-mode (low-latency chat -> Hosted/Dedicated; PHI/regulatory -> Private; batch embeddings -> Dedicated). Could be 3x2 grid.

Jon Patel: Perfect. Also add a one-line inbound routing instruction for SDRs: tag leads with #enterprise-secure and route to AE team B. That helps ops and partners.

Maya Chen: Yes, include exact comms: "If customer requires on-prem or VPC + SOC2, tag #enterprise-secure and set priority = high."

Priya Nair: Copy ideas for the security stanza: short bullets only. Example: "- Data encryption in transit & at rest; customer KMS support
- Audit logs & retention options
- Option for air-gapped Private deployment" Keep each bullet 5-7 words.

Evan Li: For SLA, propose: "99.9% uptime SLA for Dedicated, predictable throughput via reserved capacity, can configure burst policies." One line.

Maya Chen: We also want a one-row benchmark narrative box: "Real customer example: 500 qps embeddings with 30% cost reduction vs naive API" — but only if legal ok. If not, use anonymized: "Enterprise pilot saw 3x throughput improvement for reranking workloads."

Alex G: I can write the anonymized micro-case. Also we should include a tiny snippet for AEs to copy into email:```
Subject: Quick note on secure inference options
Hi <Name>,
We support hosted inference for rapid pilots, Dedicated capacity for predictable SLAs, and Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) for regulated workloads. Can we show a 20-minute demo? 
Regards, <AE name>
```

Priya Nair: Love the snippet. Make sure CTA link points to the benchmark assets: https://go.redwood.ai/secure-bench (placeholder).

Maya Chen: Owners: Alex -> copy + layout, Evan -> benchmark wording + approvals from infra, Jon -> inbound routing line + AE snippet polishing, Priya -> security bullets + legal check. Deadline: EOD Thursday.

deploy-bot: New doc created: https://docs.redwood.ai/marketing/field-pocket-sheet-draft (auto-note)

Jon Patel: Quick question — how do we visually distinguish deploy-mode icons? Simple: 3 icons (cloud, shield, server-rack) with a 1-line caption each. No diagrams.

Priya Nair: Agreed. Keep color palette safe for security audiences (navy + gray).

Maya Chen: OK team — I'll compile the assets for a Friday review. If we can get legal sign-off on the anonymized benchmark by Wednesday, we can launch the asset next week. :rocket: 

Evan Li: I'll ping infra for a quick confirm on phrasing.

Alex G: Uploading first draft to the doc now, will ping here when done.

Maya Chen: Thanks — great progress. Small ask: include a 1-sentence "how to route inbound leads" at the bottom (exact tags + priority).

Jon Patel: Noted — I'll add the precise tag and create the routing play in Zendesk after we finalize copy.

Maya Chen: End of thread — collating comments into the doc.
